title: Cabazitaxel + prednisolone
context_label: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer after docetaxel
indication_text: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer after docetaxel
purpose: Help control advanced prostate cancer after docetaxel and relieve symptoms.
schedule_summary: Cabazitaxel is given by drip over one hour on Day 1 every 21 days, with prednisolone 10 mg daily. Treatment continues while helpful and tolerable; six cycles is not a fixed maximum.
administration_text: The unit gives chlorphenamine 10 mg IV, dexamethasone 8 mg IV and famotidine 20 mg IV at least 30 minutes before the infusion. Take prednisolone continuously as prescribed, with food. Do not stop suddenly when chemotherapy is delayed. Ask for a steroid alert card, an illness plan and advice if vomiting prevents you keeping tablets down.
monitoring_summary: Full blood count weekly during the first cycle, then before every cycle. Kidney and liver tests before each cycle; review infection, diarrhoea, hydration and numbness.
safety_note: Call your oncology team immediately for fever, shaking chills, feeling suddenly unwell, unusual bleeding or persistent vomiting/diarrhoea. Follow your own temperature and contact plan. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or new leg weakness with bladder/bowel changes: call 112/999.
urgent_extra: Call your oncology team immediately for fever, shaking chills, feeling suddenly unwell, unusual bleeding or persistent vomiting/diarrhoea. Follow your own temperature and contact plan. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or new leg weakness with bladder/bowel changes: call 112/999.

teachback: Explain the treatment schedule, steroid instructions, tests and symptoms that mean you should call.

Discuss alternatives, likely benefit and uncertainty, possible lasting or fatal effects, fertility, contraception and your priorities.

agents.name: Cabazitaxel
agents.mechanism: Cabazitaxel stabilises microtubules, the structures cells need to divide. This disrupts cancer-cell division and can remain active after docetaxel, although it also affects healthy rapidly dividing cells.
agents.explanation: Cabazitaxel stabilises microtubules, the structures cells need to divide. This disrupts cancer-cell division and can remain active after docetaxel, although it also affects healthy rapidly dividing cells.
risks: Low white cells: infection, neutropenic sepsis and possible death
Low red cells: fatigue or breathlessness; low platelets: bruising or bleeding
Allergic infusion reactions, occasionally severe or life-threatening
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation, sore mouth and reduced appetite
Tiredness, hair loss, taste changes, skin and nail effects
Nerve damage: tingling, numbness or weakness, sometimes lasting
Liver abnormalities; rare serious bowel inflammation, bleeding or perforation
Fluid retention and swelling; rare lung inflammation or serious breathing problems
Kidney failure, often associated with dehydration, infection or urinary obstruction
agents.watch: Collect the prescribed diarrhoea medicine before the first cycle. The team considers white-cell growth-factor support (G-CSF), particularly with higher infection risk. Contact the team early for diarrhoea, fever, abdominal pain or reduced urine.

agents.name: Prednisolone
agents.mechanism: A prescribed steroid given continuously with this chemotherapy regimen; it can help symptoms and has its own safety and withdrawal plan.
agents.explanation: A prescribed steroid given continuously with this chemotherapy regimen; it can help symptoms and has its own safety and withdrawal plan.
risks: Raised glucose, infection risk, appetite changes, mood and sleep effects
Stomach irritation, bone loss and adrenal insufficiency if stopped abruptly
agents.watch: Take prednisolone continuously as prescribed, with food. Do not stop suddenly when chemotherapy is delayed. Ask for a steroid alert card, an illness plan and advice if vomiting prevents you keeping tablets down.

anatomy: Hair loss and fatigue are common concerns. Discuss scalp care, activity and practical support.
Use gentle mouth care. Pain, ulcers or difficulty eating/drinking needs early advice.
Call immediately for fever or sudden illness, bleeding, bruising or marked breathlessness.
Tell staff during an infusion reaction. New cough or breathlessness needs prompt review.
Keep liver tests. Yellow eyes/skin or dark urine needs urgent contact.
Persistent diarrhoea/vomiting, severe pain or blood in stool needs urgent advice.
Report tingling, numbness or weakness before each dose; symptoms can persist.
Report severe rash, nail changes or swelling. Blistering/peeling skin needs urgent assessment.

items.title: How it works
items.text: Cabazitaxel stabilises microtubules, the structures cells need to divide. This disrupts cancer-cell division and can remain active after docetaxel, although it also affects healthy rapidly dividing cells.

items.title: Radiotherapy
items.text: External-beam radiotherapy may be used for local disease control or symptoms according to the disease setting. Radium-223 is a systemic bone-targeted radiopharmaceutical and is not interchangeable with external-beam treatment.

items.title: Evidence in this setting
items.text: In TROPIC, 755 people with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer previously treated with docetaxel received cabazitaxel 25 mg/m² or mitoxantrone, both with prednisone. Median overall survival was 15.1 versus 12.7 months; hazard ratio 0.70 (95% CI 0.59–0.83). This historical comparison does not predict one person’s survival or compare all modern alternatives.

items.text: Explain that the NCCP alternative starting dose of 20 mg/m² is an unlicensed posology in Ireland and needs a documented prescribing/consent decision. Discuss alternatives, likely benefit and uncertainty, possible lasting or fatal effects, fertility, contraception and your priorities.

items.title: Fertility
items.text: Discuss fertility preservation before starting. Men should use effective contraception during treatment and for four months afterwards, according to the current product information.

items.title: Your priorities
items.text: Discuss treatment burden, likely benefit, alternatives including supportive care, and choosing to decline or stop treatment.

evidence.title: TROPIC
evidence.intro: Trial results describe groups and cannot predict an individual outcome.
evidence.population: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer after docetaxel
evidence.interpretation: In TROPIC, 755 people with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer previously treated with docetaxel received cabazitaxel 25 mg/m² or mitoxantrone, both with prednisone. Median overall survival was 15.1 versus 12.7 months; hazard ratio 0.70 (95% CI 0.59–0.83). This historical comparison does not predict one person’s survival or compare all modern alternatives.
limitations: Historical comparisons may not reflect modern previous treatment or available alternatives.
Do not extrapolate outcomes across hormone-sensitive, castration-resistant and nonmetastatic disease.
